topics.context:
8 References

This section is informative.

8.1 General References

[A-130] OMB Circular A-130, Managing Federal Information as a Strategic Resource, July 28, 2016, available at: https://obamawhitehouse.archives.gov/sites/default/files/omb/assets/OMB/circulars/a130/a130revised.pdf.

[EO 13681] Executive Order 13681, Improving the Security of Consumer Financial Transactions, October 17, 2014, available at: https://www.federalregister.gov/d/2014-25439.

[ESIG] Federal CIO Council, Use of Electronic Signatures in Federal Organization Transactions, January 25, 2013, available at: https://cio.gov/wp-content/uploads/downloads/2014/03/Use_of_ESignatures_in_Federal_Agency_Transactions_v1-0_20130125.pdf.

[FISMA] Federal Information Security Modernization Act of 2014, available at: https://www.congress.gov/bill/113th-congress/senate-bill/2521.

[HSPD-12] Department of Homeland Security, Homeland Security Presidential Directive 12: Policy for a Common Identification Standard for Federal Employees and Contractors, August 27, 2004, available at: https://www.dhs.gov/homeland-security-presidential-directive-12.

[M-03-22] OMB Memorandum M-03-22, OMB Guidance for Implementing the Privacy Provisions of the E-Government Act of 2002, September 26, 2003, available at: https://georgewbush-whitehouse.archives.gov/omb/memoranda/m03-22.html.

[M-04-04] OMB Memorandum M-04-04, E-Authentication Guidance for Federal Agencies, December 16, 2003, available at: https://georgewbush-whitehouse.archives.gov/omb/memoranda/fy04/m04-04.pdf.

[NISTIR8062] NIST Internal Report 8062, An Introduction to Privacy Engineering and Risk Management in Federal Systems, January 2017, available at: http://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/ir/2017/NIST.IR.8062.pdf.

[NIST RMF] Risk Management Framework Overview, available at http://csrc.nist.gov/groups/SMA/fisma/framework.html.

[RFC 5280] IETF, Internet X.509 Public Key Infrastructure Certificate and CRL Profile, RFC 5280, DOI 10.17487/RFC5280, May 2008, https://doi.org/10.17487/RFC5280.

[Steiner] Steiner, Peter. “On the Internet, nobody knows you’re a dog”, The New Yorker, July 5, 1993.

faqs.question: What is the purpose of OMB Circular A-130?
faqs.answer: OMB Circular A-130, titled "Managing Federal Information as a Strategic Resource," was issued on July 28, 2016, and provides guidance on managing federal information.

faqs.question: Where can I find the text of Executive Order 13681?
faqs.answer: Executive Order 13681, "Improving the Security of Consumer Financial Transactions," was issued on October 17, 2014, and is available at https://www.federalregister.gov/d/2014-25439.

faqs.question: What does the Federal CIO Council document on electronic signatures cover?
faqs.answer: The Federal CIO Council document titled "Use of Electronic Signatures in Federal Organization Transactions" was published on January 25, 2013, and can be accessed at https://cio.gov/wp-content/uploads/downloads/2014/03/Use_of_ESignatures_in_Federal_Agency_Transactions_v1-0_20130125.pdf.

faqs.question: What is the Federal Information Security Modernization Act of 2014?
faqs.answer: The Federal Information Security Modernization Act of 2014 is a federal law, and its text can be found at https://www.congress.gov/bill/113th-congress/senate-bill/2521.

faqs.question: What does HSPD-12 address?
faqs.answer: HSPD-12, issued by the Department of Homeland Security on August 27, 2004, is titled "Homeland Security Presidential Directive 12: Policy for a Common Identification Standard for Federal Employees and Contractors" and is available at https://www.dhs.gov/homeland-security-presidential-directive-12.

faqs.question: What guidance does OMB Memorandum M-03-22 provide?
faqs.answer: OMB Memorandum M-03-22, dated September 26, 2003, offers guidance for implementing the privacy provisions of the E‑Government Act of 2002 and can be accessed at https://georgewbush-whitehouse.archives.gov/omb/memoranda/m03-22.html.

faqs.question: Where can I read the NIST Internal Report 8062?
faqs.answer: NIST Internal Report 8062, titled "An Introduction to Privacy Engineering and Risk Management in Federal Systems," was published in January 2017 and is available at http://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/ir/2017/NIST.IR.8062.pdf.

faqs.question: What is RFC 5280 about?
faqs.answer: RFC 5280, published by the IETF in May 2008, is titled "Internet X.509 Public Key Infrastructure Certificate and CRL Profile" and can be found at https://doi.org/10.17487/RFC5280.

summary.title: References Section Overview
summary.long_summary:
The section titled "8 References" provides a curated list of key federal documents, executive orders, memoranda, and standards that underpin the policies and procedures discussed in the preceding sections. It is organized into a general references subsection, enumerating a variety of authoritative sources. The references include:

1. **OMB Circular A‑130** – Managing Federal Information as a Strategic Resource, dated July 28, 2016, which outlines the management of federal information assets.
2. **Executive Order 13681** – Improving the Security of Consumer Financial Transactions, issued October 17, 2014, focusing on the protection of consumer financial data.
3. **Federal CIO Council Guidance on Electronic Signatures** – Use of Electronic Signatures in Federal Organization Transactions, January 25, 2013, detailing the use of e‑signatures.
4. **Federal Information Security Modernization Act of 2014 (FISMA)** – Legislative framework for federal information security.
5. **HSPD‑12** – Homeland Security Presidential Directive 12, establishing a common identification standard for federal employees and contractors, dated August 27, 2004.
6. **OMB Memorandum M‑03‑22** – Guidance for implementing the privacy provisions of the E‑Government Act of 2002, dated September 26, 2003.
7. **OMB Memorandum M‑04‑04** – E‑Authentication Guidance for Federal Agencies, dated December 16, 2003.
8. **NIST Internal Report 8062** – An Introduction to Privacy Engineering and Risk Management in Federal Systems, January 2017.
9. **NIST Risk Management Framework Overview** – Provides an overview of the NIST RMF used for federal risk management.
10. **RFC 5280** – IETF standard for Internet X.509 Public Key Infrastructure Certificate and CRL Profile, May 2008.
11. **Steiner, Peter** – A New Yorker article titled "On the Internet, nobody knows you’re a dog," July 5, 1993, included as a cultural reference.

Each reference is accompanied by a hyperlink to the official source, ensuring that readers can access the original documents for deeper understanding. The section is marked as informative, indicating that it serves as a supporting resource rather than a directive. This compilation reflects the breadth of federal guidance on information management, security, privacy, authentication, and identity, providing a foundational backdrop for the policies and procedures detailed elsewhere in the document.
